question.problem: Use Green's theorem to evaluate ${∮}_{C}xy\,dx+(2{x}^{2}+y)\,dy,$ where $C$ is the boundary of the rectangle with vertices at $(-1,0),$ $(3,0),$ $(3,2)$ and $(-1,2).$
question.worked_solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing $D$, then Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dx+Q\,dy={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14120089/assets/3954846460076fa1ef1e5826d32bde9145e7350cb2324072b001d8c6ff41cc14.png)

We have that $P(x,y)=xy$ and $Q(x,y)=2{x}^{2}+y.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂y}=x,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂x} & =4x.\end{aligned}
$$

We can express the region $D$ as a type I region as follows:

$$
D={(x,y):-1\le x\le 3,\,0\le y\le 2}
$$

Therefore, applying Green's Theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}xy\,dx+(2{x}^{2}+y)\,dy & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(4x-x)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}3x\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}3x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{3}3x[y]_{0}^{2}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{3}3x(2)\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{3}6x\,dx \\  & =3[{x}^{2}]_{-1}^{3} \\  & =3[9-1] \\  & =24.\end{aligned}
$$
